claims.text: Ultrasonic burnishing of a FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix will improve its overall wear resistance relative to an untreated coating across varied thermal and contact regimes.
The target material is a FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix.
Ultrasonic burnishing induces severe plastic deformation in the coating.
Ultrasonic burnishing causes grain refinement in the coating.
Ultrasonic burnishing causes dislocation accumulation in the coating.
Grain refinement and dislocation accumulation increase coating hardness.
The resulting increase in hardness enhances wear resistance.
Ultrasonic burnishing will reduce the coating's wear rate relative to an untreated FeNiCrCoCu coating on Cu.
The wear-rate decrease will be at least 60%.
Similar studies have observed a wear-rate decrease of at least 60% following ultrasonic burnishing.
The magnitude of the wear-resistance improvement may depend on operating conditions and ultrasonic-burnishing parameters.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in wear rate relative to the untreated control will reject the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary predicts at least a 60% wear-rate reduction, but the rejection rule only requires a statistically significant reduction. A smaller significant reduction would violate the quantitative prediction while not falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
